text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: inference-service 5xx spike > 3% for 5m (severity: high). Auto-attach: #oncall-bridge.

alice (oncall): acked. I'm on the bridge. Seeing a spike in 5xx and a handful of timeouts to the GPU pool. No deploys in the last 30m.

ben (eng-sre): joining. Can you paste the top errors?

alice (oncall): quick tail from the logs:
```
ERROR inference-runtime: kv-cache: key-miss exception: connection reset by peer
ERROR http: upstream returned 503 for /v1/generate
WARNING autoscaler: scale_down_reject: busy_nodes > 0
```

carla (serving): we started seeing high KV eviction rates from the new trie cache change earlier this week, could be related. Dmitri, any network blips in the cluster?

dmitri (platform): infra metrics look nominal for host networking. No cloud-network deploys. I see increased GC on the model-runtime pods though. Possible memory pressure causing OOM-kills?

alice (oncall): for immediate mitigation I'm going to enable the soft-fallback route to model-variant:llm-small for non-critical routes and scale the inference-pool. Will also disable KV caching for the affected pool.

ben (eng-sre): sounds good. Commands I ran:
```
kubectl -n inference scale statefulset/inference-pool --replicas=10
kubectl -n inference patch cm inference-runtime --patch '{"data":{"kv_cache_enabled":"false"}}'
```
Response: pods came up in ~45s, tail errors dropped to ~0.9%.

alice (oncall): routing change: enabled fallback (routes/priority) at 12:07 UTC. Latency for routed requests went up a bit but error rate dropped. Customers on dedicated plans unaffected.

ops-bot: Event: fallback-route toggled by alice (oncall) at 12:07 UTC.

carla (serving): confirm if the cache eviction patch was the root cause — we should revert the trie change on staging and run the load test. I'll open a PR to revert the config.

sre-lead: good containment. Next steps: schedule post-incident review, collect metrics (5xx by route, pod restarts, kv eviction counts), and define action items.

alice (oncall): handoff: I'm stepping off the bridge in 30m to hand to ben. Ben, can you run the deeper investigation and own the postmortem?

ben (eng-sre): taking ownership. I'll run heap profiles and look at the runtime's memory alloc patterns. Also want to correlate autoscaler decisions with traffic spikes.

carla (serving): I will revert the trie change in staging now and run the synthetic "long-conversation" load. PR: https://git.internal/repo/serving/PR-4521

ben (eng-sre): collecting traces and will attach to the postmortem doc: https://redwood.atlassian.com/secure/incident/INC-2026-1938421

alice (oncall): on-call notes:
- Containment: fallback enabled and kv-cache disabled for pool A.
- Customer impact: ~1.1% of requests returned 5xx during the 12:00–12:20 window. Affected customers: a small subset on hosted API; no Dedicated contract violations.
- Mitigation window: 12:05–12:22 UTC.

ops-bot: Bridge closed by alice (oncall) at 12:35 UTC.

ben (eng-sre): post-incident meeting scheduled for 2026-04-02 09:00 UTC. I created the postmortem page and initial timeline. Link above.

sre-lead: Action items (from the bridge) — adding owners and target dates: 
1) carla: revert trie-cache change on staging and validate (due 2026-03-20) :mag:
2) ben: run heap/alloc diffs and correlate with node-level OOMs (due 2026-03-22) :test_tube:
3) dmitri: add node-level continuous GC and memory-surge synthetic check to monitoring (due 2026-03-25) :bar_chart:
4) sres: refine SLO alerting to separate 5xx volume vs % (ben + alice, due 2026-03-24)
5) carla + platform: add an autoscaler safety check to avoid aggressive scale-down during eviction storms (due 2026-03-30)

alice (oncall): putting the action items in the tracker now. Quick note on SLOs: current alert triggers at 1% 5xx across all routes. That lumps noisy low-volume routes with high-volume ones. We should change to per-route thresholds + an aggregated rolling-window so can avoid noisy pages.

ben (eng-sre): agreed. Proposal: two-tier alerts: per-route 5xx > 2% for >5m AND cluster-wide 5xx > 0.7% for >3m. Also add a suppression period for known deploy windows.

carla (serving): also recommend a new synthetic that runs a 60s conversational stream to exercise KV caching and check for increased miss/eviction rates. If miss_rate > 0.5% then page SRE with a lower severity.

dmitri (platform): for paging noise: adding a dedupe rule for the incident-bot to collapse repeated 5xx alerts within 2m for the same pod set. That should reduce duplicate pages during noisy spikes.

ben (eng-sre): we should also add an automated rollback or quick-fallback play in the runbook for cache-config changes. Example snippet to rollback config in <2m:
```
# revert config and restart pool
kubectl -n inference set env ds/inference-runtime KV_CACHE_MODE=legacy
kubectl -n inference rollout restart statefulset/inference-pool
```

alice (oncall): postmortem draft checklist (adding to page): timeline, customer impact, RCA, action items, mitigation effectiveness, changelog of config. I'll assign reviewers: carla, dmitri, sre-lead.

sre-lead: monitoring follow-ups (I will own):
- split 5xx alerts as discussed; add per-route dims.
- create an alert that monitors pod restart rate spikes tied to GC pauses.
- set up a 15m quiet window for non-critical alert types around deploys.

carla (serving): FYI: PR to revert trie change has been merged to staging, running canary load now. Results preliminary: no elevated eviction after revert.

ben (eng-sre): great. Early hypothesis: trie change increased memory churn -> more GC -> higher evictions -> kv-cache exceptions -> upstream 503s. We'll validate with heap diffs.

alice (oncall): final handoff: ben will take the investigation; I will mark the incident as contained and update the oncall log.

ben (eng-sre): owning follow-ups. I'll post a TL;DR to #product-updates after the postmortem is ready.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1938421 status updated: contained -> postmortem_pending.

sre-lead: before we close, two quick decisions:
- change SLO alerting rule to per-route + cluster aggregate (ben/alice to implement).
- add the synthetic KV workload check to CI (carla/dmitri to implement).

carla (serving): assigning myself the revert validation and the synthetic test.

ben (eng-sre): assigning myself the memory-profile analysis and SLO alert changes.

alice (oncall): thanks everyone. Follow-ups will be tracked in the incident page and in the action tracker. Please update your action items by the due dates. :white_check_mark:

sre-lead: closing notes: good containment and quick routing decision. We need to reduce alert noise and make the autoscaler more robust to eviction storms. We'll review in the postmortem.

(End of thread)
